plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: bidding higher risks paying more than your value if you win against a bid between your value and your bid, while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since I have no information suggesting otherwise (first round, no history), I will bid exactly my value of $30 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction with independent private values. In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: it guarantees you win whenever your value exceeds the highest competing bid, and you never overpay since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own. Bidding above value risks paying more than the item is worth; bidding below value risks losing profitable wins. With no prior history to exploit, truthful bidding is optimal.

In a second-price auction, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. This is because I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid. Bidding my true value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the competition (capturing positive profit) and avoid winning when it would result in a loss. Overbidding risks paying more than my value; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $6, I will bid $6.
